GitHub repo https://github.com/LayerZero-Labs/LayerZero-v2 confirmed. The README explicitly states the protocol is 'immutable, censorship-resistant, and permissionless'. Deployment artifacts are not stored in the repo directly; the canonical source is the metadata API. Docs confirm contracts are immutable and non-upgradeable.

Multi-chain enumeration completed via the deployments metadata API. 131 active mainnet V2 deployments catalogued. Key finding: EndpointV2 address 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c is shared across virtually all EVM chains (Ethereum eid 30101, Base eid 30184, Arbitrum eid 30110, Polygon eid 30109, Avalanche eid 30106, BSC eid 30102, Optimism eid 30111, and ~120 more). SendUln302/ReceiveUln302/Executor addresses vary per chain.

No factory pattern detected. LayerZero V2 deploys individual EndpointV2, SendUln302, ReceiveUln302, Executor, ReadLib1002, and BlockedMessageLib contracts per chain. No allPools/getPool/getMarket enumeration applicable.

Role taxonomy applied: EndpointV2 = other (protocol entry/exit point); SendUln302/ReceiveUln302 = other (message libraries); ReadLib1002 = other (lzRead library); LZ Executor = other (auto-executor); DeadDVN = other (placeholder for unconfigured pathways); BlockedMessageLib = other (pathway disabler). No multisig, timelock, or governor addresses surfaced from the metadata API; owner/admin addresses for the immutable contracts are not enumerated in the public metadata.

All addresses in admin_addresses[] trace to the fetched metadata API response (https://metadata.layerzero-api.com/v1/metadata/deployments) which was directly fetched in this run. Ethereum block explorer verification for 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fE728c was not performed due to fetch budget constraints; recorded as D8 unknown.

protocol_metadata.about: LayerZero V2 is an immutable, permissionless cross-chain messaging protocol that deploys endpoint contracts on each supported blockchain. Developers send arbitrary messages, transfer tokens via OFT (Omnichain Fungible Token) standard, or read state from other chains using lzRead. Messages are verified by configurable Decentralized Verifier Networks (DVNs) and delivered by off-chain Executors. The protocol's design is explicitly non-upgradeable: once deployed, endpoint and message library contracts cannot be changed, and OApp owners configure their own security stack by selecting DVNs per pathway.
